stories.headline: 2026 NFL trade deadline updates: Jordan Davis, Andre Cisco on the move
stories.summary: The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. We're following all the action, including Jessie Bates III, Davon Godchaux and Jordan Davis to the Jaguars.
stories.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. We already have seen double-digit deals -- and more are on the way on the final day.

On Monday, the Jaguars traded for safety Jessie Bates III, defensive tackle Davon Godchaux and defensive tackle Jordan Davis. The Lions also added safety help with Andre Cisco. Other big names to be dealt so far include Jeffery Simmons to the Bears, J.J. McCarthy to the Giants, Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens and Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys.

We're tracking all in-season moves and trade-related buzz right through the deadline. The most recent deals and intel will be added at the top.

More coverage:

Transactions | Depth charts

Grading every big trade

Follow the latest deals, intel before the deadline

Nov. 4

Cardinals trade QB Brissett to Ravens
Ravens get: QB Jacoby Brissett, 2027 fifth-round pick

Cardinals get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 seventh-round pick

The Cardinals finalized a trade to send QB Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens on Friday. The Cardinals are sending a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-rounder in exchange for Brissett and a 2027 fourth-round selection.

Brissett's first start as the Ravens' starting quarterback could come as soon as Week 10 when Baltimore hosts the Chargers on "Monday Night Football." He was recently benched by the Cardinals before the trade.

Walder: Grading the deal from both sides
Hensley: Can Brissett save the Ravens?

Oct. 29

Titans trade DT Simmons to Bears
Bears get: DT Jeffery Simmons, 2028 fifth-round pick

Titans get: 2027 first-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 first-round pick

The Bears are acquiring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Titans, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter. The Titans are receiving 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, plus a 2027 fourth-round pick from the Bears in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick, the sources told Schefter.

Simmons, 29, signed a three-year, $105.8 million extension with $100 million guaranteed with the Titans in June. He is under contract through the 2030 season.

Walder: Grading the deal from both sides
Staff: Answering big questions on the deal
Barnwell: Does trading two first-rounders work?

Oct. 27

Colts trade DT Buckner to 49ers
49ers get: DT DeForest Buckner

Colts get: 2027 fourth-round pick

The Colts are trading three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to the 49ers, the team that made him a 2016 first-round pick before dealing him to Indianapolis in 2020, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

The Colts will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from the 49ers, sources said.

Walder: Grading the deal from both sides
Wagoner: Are the 49ers stopping at Buckner?

Colts trade G Nelson to Seahawks
Seahawks get: G Quenton Nelson

Colts get: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

The Colts have agreed to trade eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Nelson is on an expiring contract, and the Colts are opting to get back draft capital now before they could lose him in free agency.

Walder: Grading the deal from both sides
Staff: Answering big questions on the deal

Oct. 11

Cardinals trade WR Harrison to Texans
Texans get: WR Marvin Harrison Jr., 2027 seventh-round pick

Cardinals get: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pick

The Texans have completed a trade for Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters. The Texans sent 2027 second- and sixth-round draft picks to the Cardinals for Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round selection, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Harrison reunites with his former Ohio State QB C.J. Stroud in Houston.

Walder: Grading the deal from both sides
Weinfuss: Why the Cardinals moved on
Staff: Answering big questions on the deal
Barnwell: Why'd the Texans make this trade?

Oct. 7

Eagles trade C Jurgens to Ravens
Eagles get: 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Ravens get: C Cam Jurgens, 2027 seventh-round pick

The Eagles are trading two-time Pro Bowl center Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Ravens in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Wednesday.

The Eagles had moved Jurgens to left guard after Landon Dickerson was placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Jurgens self-reported concussion symptoms Monday morning, was evaluated and is now in the concussion protocol, a source told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo on Monday.

Walder: Grading the deal from both sides

Sept. 30

Steelers trade CB Porter to Cowboys
Steelers get: 2027 sixth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Cowboys get: CB Joey Porter Jr.

The Steelers are trading Porter to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round selection, sources confirmed to NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe and ESPN's Todd Archer.

The trade marks the end of a monthslong saga that stretched throughout the Steelers' offseason as Porter, one of the team's 2023 second-round picks, awaited an extension and was sidelined with a back injury.

Staff: Answering big questions on the deal

Sept. 28

Vikings trade QB McCarthy to Giants
Giants get: QB J.J. McCarthy

Vikings get: 2027 fifth-round pick

The Giants traded for Vikings quarterback McCarthy on Monday, sending a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to Minnesota for the 2024 first-round pick. McCarthy, taken by the Vikings with the No. 10 pick, was the third-string quarterback in Minnesota behind starter Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz.

Giants coach John Harbaugh said after their Week 3 victory over the Titans that Jameis Winston would remain the Giants' starter even if the team added another quarterback. He reiterated that Monday after the trade for McCarthy.

stories.headline: NHL Awards Watch: Believe it or not, McDavid not the unanimous MVP pick right now
stories.summary: Our panel of PHWA voters identify their finalists for all the awards, with some tight races in a few spots.
stories.body:
There are clear favorites for NHL awards after the first month-plus of the regular season -- and some of them don't actually play for the Edmonton Oilers.

Yes, Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard had proved to be undeniable awards contenders out of the gate. But it's also undeniable that front-runners at the start of the season might not be the players holding trophies at the end of the season.

Welcome to the NHL Awards Watch for November. We've polled a wide selection of Professional Hockey Writers Association voters anonymously to get a sense of where the wind is blowing for the current leaders. We've made sure it's a cross section from the entire league, trying to gain as many perspectives as possible.

Keep in mind that the PHWA votes for the Hart, Norris, Calder, Selke and Lady Byng finalists, broadcasters vote for the Jack Adams and general managers vote for the Vezina.

All stats are from Hockey-Reference.com, Natural Stat Trick and Evolving Hockey.

Jump ahead:

Ross | Richard | Hart

Norris | Selke | Vezina

Calder | Byng | Adams

Art Ross Trophy (points leader)
Click here for the updated point-scoring standings.

Maurice 'Rocket' Richard Trophy
Click here for the updated goal-scoring standings.

Hart Trophy (MVP)
Leader: Connor McDavid, Edmonton Oilers

Finalists: Kirill Kaprizov, Minnesota Wild; Nathan MacKinnon, Colorado Avalanche

"Duh."

"Really, is there anyone else?"

"He's the clear front-runner and it's not close."

Yes, the reviews are in for McDavid's first several weeks of the 2026-27 season. The Oilers' star earned just over 88% of the first-place votes on our MVP ballots.

McDavid is seeking his fourth Hart Trophy and first since 2023, which is an odd gap in MVP honors for a player who is constantly in the conversation. Only three players in NHL history won the Hart Trophy four times: Wayne Gretzky, as part of his NHL record nine MVP honors, as well as Gordie Howe and Eddie Shore.

The Oilers' center had 47 points in his first 18 games this season. To put that points pace into perspective: His 2.61 points-per-game average would rank as the sixth highest in a single season, with only three Gretzky campaigns and two Mario Lemieux scoring seasons ranking ahead of him. That McDavid offensive fuel has made Edmonton a top-five team since the start of the season.

As one awards voter noted: Bookmakers have "the field" at plus money vs. McDavid when it comes to the MVP race. That's how heavy a favorite he is right now.

That said, the Hart Trophy vote was not unanimous among those we surveyed.

MacKinnon received first-place support and consistent mentions lower on the ballots. The star center won the Hart in 2024 and has been a finalist five times, including a third-place finish last season. The Avalanche haven't gotten off the blocks how they wanted this season, but that's not on MacKinnon. He had 30 points through 18 games, seven more than any other teammate.

Completing a Western Conference sweep of the Hart finalists: Wild winger Kaprizov. He had 31 points through 19 games to start the season, and his 16 goals were near the top of that leaderboard. His line with Joel Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy has been the best in the league, rolling to nearly five goals per 60 minutes at 5-on-5 while not surrendering an even-strength goal through 19 games.

Kaprizov has never been a Hart Trophy finalist in his career, and has finished in the top 10 in MVP voting only once in six seasons. Like MacKinnon, he had first-place support and a ton of love down the ballot.

"I wouldn't bet against Kirill Kaprizov narrowing the gap as the season goes along," one McDavid voter warned.

Another name mentioned by our MVP voters was Edmonton's Evan Bouchard ... but we believe he has designs on another trophy at the moment.

Norris Trophy (top defenseman)
Leader: Evan Bouchard, Edmonton Oilers

Finalist: Quinn Hughes, Vancouver Canucks; Zach Werenski, Columbus Blue Jackets

Bouchard is the runaway favorite for the Norris right now with over 83% of the first-place votes, for the same reason McDavid is leading for the Hart: At some point, the stats just become undeniable.

The Oilers' defenseman had 31 points through his first 18 games, following a dominating 95-point season in 2025-26. He had a plus-25 rating last season. He's already at plus-24 this season.

"The electric offense pace is too much to ignore, even if there are still some defensive lapses," a Bouchard voter said.

Bouchard, who was fourth for the Norris last season, has faced the same obstacle that other offensive defensemen have faced in trying to win this award: whether his defensive game is Norris-worthy. The same clips of blown coverages that used to dog players such as Erik Karlsson have burned into the memories of voters when it comes to Bouchard. But that perception seems to be changing; or, at the very least, his offensive game is so overwhelming that it silences that defensive debate. (See also: Karlsson, Erik.)

"Bouchard is on pace for 67 points before Santa drops his gifts off under the tree. Plus, he isn't anywhere near the defensive liability many like to suggest," another Bouchard backer boasted.

"Bouchard has a slight edge over Quinn Hughes because of overall production. But it's hard to argue Hughes hasn't been terrific in handling a significant workload," another noted.

Hughes earned the second-most first-place votes and is the clear second choice in this race. The Norris winner in 2023, Hughes is averaging 28 minutes, 7 seconds in ice time per game for the Wild. Despite Bouchard's blockbuster offensive season, Hughes is right there with him in the scoring race among defensemen with 26 points through his first 19 games. He has been a driving force behind the Wild's successful start.

Hughes was seventh for the Norris last season, when he split his time between Minnesota and Vancouver.

"To me, he's the biggest difference-maker from the back end in the league, just dangerous in so many ways," a Hughes voter beamed.

The only other defenseman to earn a first-place vote was Werenski, who won the Norris for the first time last season. He has 14 points through 15 games, skating to a plus-6 and averaging a league-high 28:18 per game in ice time. Unlike the other two finalists here, Werenski's team is off to a disappointing start, but he has been a highlight among lowlights.

Other defensemen mentioned for the Norris by our voters included Adam Fox of the New York Rangers, Cale Makar of the Colorado Avalanche and Mikhail Sergachev of the Utah Mammoth.

Calder Trophy (top rookie)
Leader: Jacob Fowler, Montreal Canadiens

Finalists: Michael Brandsegg-Nygard, Detroit Red Wings; Roman Kantserov, Chicago Blackhawks

The Calder Trophy race has one clear favorite above a disparate collection of rookies making impacts in a variety of ways for their teams.

Let's start with the big name in flashing lights on the marquee. Fowler, 21, is a Florida native who has quickly established himself as the goalie of the future for the Montreal Canadiens ... only a few months after Montreal appeared to have found its goalie of the future.

"Wasn't the net supposed to belong to Jakub Dobes?" a Fowler voter asked.

Fowler was 8-1-1 in his first 10 games this season, with a .925 save percentage and a 2.15 goals-against average. Money Puck had him second in the NHL goals saved above expected through those games (11.4). His two shutouts led all rookie goalies. He's been phenomenal for Montreal.

The Canadiens netminder earned just over 61% of the first-place votes for the Calder. He's trying to become the first goalie to win the Calder since Steve Mason of the Blue Jackets in 2008-09. But he's also looking over his shoulder at a deep freshman class.

"This rookie race is insane," another Fowler voter declared. "Tough to pinpoint a real favorite."

Earning the second-most first-place votes: Brandsegg-Nygård of the Red Wings. The 21-year-old Norwegian was drafted 15th overall in 2024 and played 14 games with Detroit last season. This season, he had 10 points through 18 games with a three-plus minute jump in ice time.

"Even more impressive than his points was that Detroit outscored teams 12-3 with him on the ice and without him were outscored 18-27," a Brandsegg-Nygård voter explained.

The player with the next highest total of first-place votes is also a bright spot on a mediocre team: Roman Kantserov, the 22-year-old Russian-born winger for the Blackhawks. He led the KHL in goals last season before signing with the Blackhawks, who drafted him 44th overall in 2023.

He scored nine goals in his first 18 NHL games to go along with two assists. Kantserov was the leading goal scorer on the Blackhawks, who ranked last in the league offensively heading into Monday's action.

"I'm leaning toward Kantserov. He's playing big minutes and producing, albeit for a hapless Chicago team," one of his voters acknowledged.

Other rookies to get first-place votes included 2026 first overall pick Gavin McKenna of the Toronto Maple Leafs; Vegas Golden Knights forward Trevor Connelly, who's been near the top of the rookie scoring leaders; Boston Bruins forward James Hagens, another name near the top of the scoring leaderboard who has produced solid numbers in limited minutes; and Rangers goalie Dylan Garand, who was thrust into action when Igor Shesterkin was lost for the season to a knee injury.

Vezina Trophy (top goaltender)
Note: The NHL's general managers vote for this award.

Leader: Jesper Wallstedt, Minnesota Wild

Finalists: Pyotr Kochetkov, Carolina Hurricanes; Linus Ullmark, Ottawa Senators

Wallstedt finished sixth for the Calder last season but is the current leader for the Vezina among our voters. The "Wall of St. Paul" is 11-2-3 in his first 16 games, with a .922 save percentage and a 1.99 goals-against average; analytically, Money Puck has Wallstedt as the league leader in goals saved above expected (13.3) through 16 games.

"He's been outstanding while facing a lot of quality chances," a voter noted.

"Wallstedt is my front-runner right now. He's been a workhorse and has backed it up (two or fewer goals allowed in 11 of 16 starts)," another stated.

Wallstedt earned around 58% of the first-place votes. The next-highest total belonged to Kochetkov, who has put up stellar numbers while starting 12 of the Hurricanes' 19 games. The 27-year-old might be finally breaking through after several seasons in the Canes' goaltending mix. He has a .920 save percentage and a 1.67 goals-against average through 12 games.

The goalie with the next-most first-place votes is Linus Ullmark of the Senators. But, admittedly, this was a surprise given that he's been limited to just eight games due to injury. But within those eight games, no one was better this season: 7-1-0 with a .945 save percentage and a 1.33 goals-against average.

"Linus Ullmark probably would be the leader here if not for the injury he suffered," a Wallstedt voter argued.

Only one other goalie received first-place support from our voters: Boston Bruins netminder Jeremy Swayman. He's 9-3-1 in 13 games this season, with a .920 save percentage and a 2.21 goals-against average. Swayman was a finalist for this award last season.

"This is Swayman at his best. No way Boston is this good out of the gate without him playing at this level," a Swayman backer declared.

Other goalies who received support down the ballot included Montreal's Jacob Fowler and Dallas' Jake Oettinger.

Selke Trophy (best defensive forward)
Leader: Joel Eriksson Ek, Minnesota Wild

Finalists: Anthony Cirelli, Tampa Bay Lightning; Nick Suzuki, Montreal Canadiens

It's been a minute since Eriksson Ek was a Selke darling. After finishing fourth for the award in 2021, he was outside the top 10 finishers for the award in the last two seasons. Naturally, he's the early leader for the defensive forward award while having one of his best offensive starts, because that's how the Selke works. Eriksson Ek has 17 points in 19 games, skating to a plus-16.

"The Wild have given up just two goals in more than 260 minutes with him on the ice at 5 on 5, and none in over 200 minutes at full strength when he's centering Kaprizov and Boldy," one voter revealed.

Eriksson Ek led the voting with 26% of the first-place votes. But as usual with the Selke, there's a robust collection of forwards that also earned first-place love.

Suzuki and Cirelli were tied with just over 15% of the first-place votes. It was Suzuki's turn to win the Selke last season, in which he also finished fifth for the Hart Trophy. He's been impactful again for the Habs despite being limited to 11 games due to injury.

If it's any player's "turn" to win the Selke this season, it might be Cirelli. He finished third in the voting in 2025 and then second to Suzuki last season.

"He's just so consistent," a Cirelli voter argued.

The only other player to receive multiple first-place votes was Sebastian Aho of the Carolina Hurricanes. Would it be weird if Jordan Staal remains without a Selke win in his career but Aho collects one instead for Carolina?

Other players receiving first-place votes were Montreal center Phillip Danault; Vegas center Jack Eichel; Dallas center Radek Faksa; Boston center Elias Lindholm; and Vancouver center Elias Pettersson. Other players that were mentioned down the ballot included New Jersey center Nico Hischier and Philadelphia forward Noah Cates.

Lady Byng Trophy (gentlemanly play)

This is the part where I mention that the Lady Byng Trophy for gentlemanly play should be voted on by the league's on-ice officials or by the NHL Players' Association instead of the PHWA. Traditionally, this award goes to a player with a top-20 point total and the lowest penalty minutes among those players.

Jack Hughes has 25 points in 18 games and has yet to take a penalty this season. Works for us.

Jack Adams Award (best coach)
Note: The NHL Broadcasters' Association votes on this award.

Leader: Marco Sturm, Boston Bruins

Finalists: Rod Brind'Amour, Carolina Hurricanes; Travis Green, Vancouver Canucks

The Bruins are one of the NHL's biggest surprises this season, and Sturm is getting much of the credit. The second-year head coach has them playing to a plus-27 goal differential and earned 58% of the first-place votes on our ballots.

"He probably should've gotten more love last year," a Sturm backer argued.

"Every year I expect the Bruins to drop off the map, but they continue to chart a course toward the playoffs. And when you look at this roster, it doesn't scream top of the Atlantic Division, and yet, here we are," another explained.

The second-most first-place votes belong to Brind'Amour, who has the Hurricanes atop the Metro Division after winning the Stanley Cup last season. They remain defensively stout, but Brind'Amour has them cooking offensively: Through 19 games, the Hurricanes led the league in goals per game.

"Is putting the defending Stanley Cup champion coach as the Jack Adams frontrunner too cliche? Oh well, I'm doing it," one voter joked.

Brind'Amour has coached through some adversity, having lost captain Jordan Staal to injury last month.

Green has coached the Senators through much more of it, from losing Brady Tkachuk to an offseason trade to a slew of injuries that befell the Ottawa roster early on this season.

Despite all that, the Senators were in a wild-card spot after 18 games.

"Ottawa keeps taking its lumps, and Green is somehow keeping them in the mix. Impressive," one voter concluded.

Two other coaches received first-place votes: Montreal Canadiens bench boss Martin St. Louis and Mike Babcock of the Edmonton Oilers.

That Babcock didn't receive more support is both surprising and unsurprising. On the one hand, he's overseen a torrid start for the Oilers in which McDavid is amassing points at a historic pace while the team plays solid defense in front of uncharacteristically strong goaltending. On the other hand, Babcock carried significant baggage into this job and the voters -- at least among the writers -- have a long memory.

"Babcock could go 84-0 and he would not get my vote," a Sturm voter revealed.

stories.headline: Virgil van Dijk: 'No panic' over uncertain Liverpool future
stories.summary: Virgil van Dijk has said he is "not in any panic" about his Liverpool future despite the fact his contract is set to expire next summer.
stories.body:
Virgil van Dijk has said he is "not in any panic" about his Liverpool future despite the fact his contract is set to expire next summer.

The 35-year-old penned a two-year extension at Anfield in April 2024 and remains an ever-present in the Reds' back line. He has played every minute for Liverpool in the Premier League this season but says he is not concerned about the prospect of his current deal running out.

"I feel good but it's not about me at the moment," Van Dijk said. "Let's see. I'm not in any panic."

"I want to keep playing and continue what I'm doing. Let's see what the season brings. I've had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that's the case.

- Alisson in talks over new Liverpool contract: 'I'm happy to stay'

- Liverpool's Barcola, Isak, Wirtz show signs they're finally starting to click

- If Arsenal find attacking spark, they could run away with the Premier League

"If not, then I will go somewhere else. There's nothing to report at the moment but that doesn't mean that there's any stress or anything."

Van Dijk has withdrawn from international duty ahead of the Netherlands' Nations League matches with Greece and Germany, having been carrying a knock during his recent outings for Liverpool.

Reflecting on the club's progress under new head coach Andoni Iraola, the defender said: "It's a work in progress. Some games we could have done much better ... And some games we lost but we were good. We're trying to find consistency as that's the only way to be successful."

stories.headline: As Jaylen Brown faces the Celtics for the first time, familiar questions linger
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown and the Philadelphia 76ers host Jayson Tatum and the Boston Celtics on Tuesday night.
stories.body:
FOR MUCH OF his decade-long career with the Boston Celtics, Jaylen Brown spent time answering questions about his role.

Critics wondered whether he and Jayson Tatum could coexist, speculated about whose team it was. Both players, their teammates and coaches were aware of the narrative.

"The media wants to kind of sometimes write the story that pulls us apart," Brown said in 2021. "But we talk a lot. We don't let it bother us."

So as Brown -- now a Philadelphia 76er after Boston traded him this offseason -- sat at Sixers media day a month ago, a reporter asked him: "Do you guys know who the alpha is?"

There were years of frustration loaded into Brown's smirk and two-word response: "Next question."

Four months into his Sixers tenure, Brown has again fielded questions about his relationship with his former running mate in Boston, partly because of a social media firestorm Brown started. It has led to back-and-forth comments between Brown and Tatum, and a report from NBC Sports and Celtics TV analyst Brian Scalabrine about Brown's "demands" and "trade request" in Boston. Scalabrine later walked back his comments about Brown asking for a trade.

A source with knowledge of the situation told ESPN that there was no truth to the report.

Instead, the source said, Brown discovered his former team had tried -- and failed -- to trade him to the Milwaukee Bucks while he was on vacation over the summer. The one thing Brown did ask for, the source said, was to be involved in the process of where he was traded. The Celtics ignored the request and sent him 300 miles southwest to Philadelphia.

So Brown finds himself in a familiar position: On a team he didn't choose laden with star power, trying to establish a role that will lead his squad to a title. On Tuesday, he and Tatum will face off for the first time as opponents -- leading the top two teams in the Eastern Conference -- as the Sixers (9-2) take on the Celtics (8-2) (8 p.m. ET, NBC).

Brown has no plans to repair the relationship -- which he said isn't beef but "lamb chops and some gravy" -- with his former co-star.

"There's nothing to talk about. I mean, he's on his side, I'm on my side," Brown said Sunday. "Both of us are trying to win, so it's nothing to talk about. Just check the ball up.

"I love Boston. Boston's a great city. A lot of people I developed a relationship with, but I'm just focused on what's in front of me right now."

BROWN WAS ON a monthlong vacation that spanned China, Africa and Europe when he learned that the Celtics had tried to trade him to the Bucks for Giannis Antetokounmpo.​

Antetokounmpo got traded to the Miami Heat on June 22, and Brown was left wondering about his future in Boston. He let the Celtics know that despite the failed trade he was willing to remain in Boston, but the team informed him he would be dealt anyway, the source told ESPN.

The team decided to trade Brown because his and Tatum's massive contracts made it difficult to build a sustained contender, general manager Brad Stevens later explained. ​

As the Celtics continued to explore the market for Brown after the failed Antetokounmpo trade, Brown asked to have a say in where he was sent or at minimum be given a heads-up on the destination. But he learned he'd be going to the Sixers only after the deal was finalized. ​

Brown reacted to the trade on his Twitch stream a day later, where he said he felt like there was a "lack of respect" for him during the process. He said he wasn't thrilled with the way Stevens "facilitated some of the conversations" but believed there was "more to it."​

"There was definitely a message being sent, and that message was received," Brown said. "I just wish the more to it could have been explained to me.

"I thought I earned respect enough to get that explanation, but obviously I was wrong." ​

The Celtics declined to comment for this story, instead pointing to Stevens' remarks on the trade. Stevens said in July that he didn't keep Tatum in the loop about trading Brown, nor did he speak with Tatum the next day.

"I didn't want to put that on him or anyone else in the playing group," Stevens said. He also said that neither the Celtics nor Brown was disgruntled with the other.​

Brown and Tatum spent nine years together in Boston, going from fledgling teenagers to one of the most successful pairings of their era, winning a title in 2024 that ended a 16-year drought for one of the league's most successful franchises.

"I think Jayson and Jaylen have had a remarkable partnership where they complemented each other great," Stevens said. ​

But when Brown and Tatum saw each other for the first time since the trade during an Oct. 10 preseason game in Boston, they acted like they didn't know each other. Tatum went through an on-court workout on Boston's home floor. Brown did the same on the other end, at times just an arm's length away from his former costar.

They never acknowledged one another, and each headed to his respective locker room.​

It was the first clear indication there was tension between these former costars, which has intensified in recent weeks.​

It all started when Brown commented with a blue hat emoji -- a symbol for "cap," slang for someone lying -- on Instagram in response to Tatum saying in a video on his YouTube channel that he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" by Brown's trade.​

"There's no beef. It's not about that. It should be more praise," Tatum said a day later. "I understand drama gets clicks and views, but I'm not really into that. I'm not blaming everybody for how they feel. Everybody is entitled to their own feelings, and we all go through different things in our lives."​​

Two days later, Brown had a different tone, insisting there was "no beef" between them but adding that there "might be a little lamb chops and some gravy." He also repeated multiple times that Tatum had a "hell of a PR team." ​​

"He should stay ready at all times," Brown added.

​Brown declined to address why he posted the cap emoji under Tatum's post, instead saying he and Tatum are focused on what's ahead. Tatum said he called and texted Brown when the trade happened and would welcome a conversation with him to hash out the potential issue. But Brown has said multiple times since that he isn't interested in speaking to Tatum.

"We both got so much stuff in front of us," Brown said. "So at the end of the day ... he got to do what he's got to do for his team. I got to do what I do for my team.​"

TYRESE MAXEY HIT a 3-pointer to cut a 29-point Cleveland Cavaliers lead to 10 during the second game of the season, which prompted a Cavs timeout. The Sixers guard walked toward the home crowd in celebration with Brown trailing close behind. The two yelled toward the Philadelphia crowd -- and the crowd yelled back.

On this team with Brown, a former Finals MVP, and LeBron James and Joel Embiid, two former NBA MVPs, it is Maxey who has been the best player and go-to scorer.

"This is his team," Brown said after a recent Sixers win over the Bulls.

Brown's willingness to take a back seat to Maxey comes as a surprise for many reasons, most notably his history. Brown wanted to be treated as an equal in Boston, a spot he seemingly believed he earned based on a decade with the team where he evolved into one of the league's best players.

Albeit early, that hasn't been the case in Philadelphia. Brown has had no desire to leave any room in Philadelphia for questions about sharing the spotlight that he faced for a decade in Boston.

So far in Philly, his transition has been without issue.

"He's been seamless," Embiid said. "I think he's adjusted pretty well."

Coach Nick Nurse has praised Brown's toughness, routinely calling him a winner. Nurse often shies away from declaring anyone on the team the alpha or go-to player but routinely mentions Brown among others when those conversations arise. In an interview with ESPN, Nurse said Brown's passion for winning -- and his championship experience -- have rubbed off on the team already.

"His teams have won at a super high clip. He plays winning basketball at both ends of the floor, and his just physical toughness are hard to find," Nurse told ESPN. "The way he cares about winning it transcends to the rest of the team just being that great a player who has that kind of mindset."

Throughout the start of the season, Brown has buoyed the Sixers in crucial moments with his defense and scoring. In that comeback win over Cleveland, for example, he scored six straight points in the fourth quarter to help put the game away. Then against the Detroit Pistons, he scored a season-high 30 points and had a game-saving block on guard Cade Cunningham.

"His stamina, his strength, his mentality is great for our ballclub," James said. "It sets the tone, and he can do it on both ends of the floor. He's one of the best, if not the best, two-way player in our game today."

Maxey echoed Nurse's and James' sentiments.

"He's something that we really needed, honestly," he said. "We like having him on our team instead of guarding him all the time."

After the Pistons game, a mob of reporters headed to Maxey, who had what was then his lowest-scoring game of the season. Brown was attempting to leave the locker room when a Sixers communications member stopped him to speak to the press; just three media members left Maxey to speak to Brown.

In many ways, the moment was a reflection of the role he's accepted in Philadelphia -- a place he never thought or asked to be -- as a willing sidekick.

"I'm the new guy here, so I'm adjusting," Brown said. "I'm just trying to complement, build off of what these guys have already built here in Philadelphia."

stories.headline: Ex-San Diego FC forward Cédric Bakambu files fair housing lawsuit
stories.summary: Former San Diego FC forward Cédric Bakambu has filed a housing discrimination lawsuit in federal court.
stories.body:
Former San Diego FC forward Cédric Bakambu has filed a housing discrimination lawsuit in federal court against one real estate firm, two property owners and two real estate agents, according to information contained in the filing.

The lawsuit, a copy of which has been viewed by ESPN, alleges the defendants discriminated against Bakambu and his wife, Anne-Laure Hueber, on the basis of "familial status" by denying them the opportunity rent a house because they had children who would be living with them.

According to the lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California, the individuals and entities listed as defendants are property owners JW Wealth and Sheila Nasehi, real estate firm Compass California III and Compass agents Gillian Gillies and Bree Bornstein.

Neither Major League Soccer nor San Diego FC are named as a defendant in the lawsuit.

Bakambu and Hueber are seeking unspecified compensatory, statutory and punitive damages, as well as declaratory and injunctive relief, attorney's fees and costs under the Fair Housing Act, the California Fair Employment and Housing Act and the Unruh Civil Rights Act.

Bakambu signed with San Diego FC back on Sept. 3, and in nine matches for SDFC, he scored four goals with one assist.

In an Instagram post dated Nov. 6, Bakambu, a Congo DR international who played at last summer's World Cup, announced that he would no longer be playing for San Diego, stating, "Some decisions are beyond our control."

A request for comment from a representative for JW Wealth wasn't successful. A request for comment from Compass was also not successful.

ESPN has asked San Diego FC, MLS and the MLS Players' Association for comment.

The suit, which was filed on Monday, alleged two instances of discrimination. In the first alleged incident, Bakambu made an offer to rent a 5,679 square-foot house in San Diego, Calif. for a monthly rent of $17,500.

The filing details how Gillies, the agent representing Compass, stated that a pool barrier "would be required due to the age of the children" and asked whether Bakambu would pay an estimated $6,000 to install it if the owner approved.

Alternatives were proposed by Bakambu's broker, Sandra Shebani, including mesh covers and splash alarms.

Gillies responded: "A barrier will need to be installed."

The requirement wasn't mentioned in the property listing.

By Sept. 16, Bakambu made an updated offer that included paying a year's rent in advance, a Pool and Spa Liability Addendum, and an agreement to pay for the barrier.

According to the filing, Compass managing director Melanie Fontana later told Shebani that another applicant that met the lease requirements was under consideration, that Bakambu's offer had been received and that the owner would fund any pool safety measures.

The lawsuit goes on to state that on Sept. 18, 2026, Ms. Shebani raised the fair-housing concern directly with Kathy Mehringer, Compass's Broker of Record and Managing Director of Compliance and Risk Management.

Mehringer responded: "Melanie has explained the process. Compass is not violating any fair housing rules - why would you accuse us of doing so? That is not collaboration."

The filing states that Bakambu's offer was never accepted, and the rental listing was withdrawn from the market after his real estate agent raised fair-housing concerns with Compass management. The suit states that by tying rental conditions to the children and their ages, Bakambu and Hueber were discriminated against.

Later, Bakambu and Hueber sought to rent a 6,300 square-foot house through Compass in Rancho Sante Fe, Calif., and on Oct. 11, 2026, after viewing the property with Bornstein, offered a monthly rent of $23,500.

The filing states: "The offer and follow-up from Ms. Hueber went unanswered even after Plaintiffs observed the home being advertised for $20,000 per month by October 26, 2026."

On Nov. 6, the rental property was taken off the market.

The suit alleges that Compass and Bornstein, its listing agent for the second property, discriminated against Bakambu and Hueber by failing to consider or negotiate their offer because of familial status, and that this was in retaliation for Bakambu and Hueber raising fair-housing concerns regarding negotiations for the first property.

While this was going on, Bakambu's family was forced to remain in temporary housing at his own expense, according to the filing.

The filing reads: "Cédric and Anne allege that this sequence was not [an] ordinary rental negotiation. They were denied equal consideration because their household included five children, and Compass subjected them to further adverse treatment after they asserted their fair-housing rights.

"The consequences were concrete: lost housing opportunities, additional expenses, prolonged housing instability, disruption of efforts to arrange schooling and activities for their children, humiliation, and emotional distress."

stories.headline: How Pat Murphy's leadership led Brewers to World Series title
stories.summary: Everyone in the Milwaukee clubhouse has their favorite Murphy story. Here are the best of the best.
stories.body:
Editor's note: This story originally ran on Oct. 27. Pat Murphy is a finalist to win the National League Manager of the Year Award announced on Nov. 10.

On orders from his manager, Milwaukee Brewers left-handed pitcher Colton Gordon headed to the upper deck of American Family Field to investigate.

After the Brewers clinched a bye in the first round of the postseason, the team held simulated games all that week in preparation for the division series. It was during one of those workouts that Brewers manager Pat Murphy asked to speak with Gordon, who was acquired from the Houston Astros in July and pitched at Triple-A until a late September call-up.

"He calls me over," Gordon recalled recently. "He says, 'This is a tight scrimmage here. We have some opposing scouts in the upper deck spying on us. We're going to send security up there. Can you give us some backup?'"

Gordon looked up where Murphy was pointing and saw a "shadowy" figure in the stands, seemingly looking down on the field. A bit confused, Gordon did as he was asked. He jumped in an elevator with a security guard, who told him he "wasn't packing," so be ready for anything.

As they approached the figure in the stands and were "ready for anything," Gordon quickly realized the joke was on him. Murphy had sent him to Section 422, where a statue of the Hall of Fame announcer Bob Uecker was waiting for him. That shadowy figure was actually a legendary one.

"I looked down, and everyone on the field is looking back up, laughing," Gordon said. "Yeah, he got me."

It's that kind of playfulness that endears the 67-year-old Murphy, who just led his team to the first World Series title in franchise history. But there's another side to the skipper. After all, this is the same manager who said he wished he could tase a player who got thrown out going from first to third.

It's the yin and yang Murphy has perfected and it leads to a question often wondered of the front-runner to win his third consecutive NL Manager of the Year award: Is it all an act?

"Every time you think it's just a ridiculous act, if you look a couple layers deep down the line, you're like, 'That wasn't just clowning around,'" a Brewers coach said. "There is something to it."

'Oh no, he's serious'

There are plenty of "Murph stories," but the current favorite of Brewers players occurred right around the start of the playoffs when he delivered a line that still has them laughing. Knowing the grind of the postseason, after playing in 162 regular-season games, he delivered an inspiring message.

"If you're tired, take a nap," reliever DL Hall recalled. "If you're weak, get stronger."

First baseman Jake Bauers said it was "the best line of all time."

It brought a laugh to the room, but it was no joke.

"Oh no, he's serious," longtime Brewers outfielder Christian Yelich said. "And when he says those things in the dugout, he means it."

Murphy isn't necessarily the type to wait until the end of the game to address a team deficiency or mistake on the field. When you come off the diamond, you'll likely hear about it immediately. And it might sound exaggerated, but there's a purpose behind it.

"I gave it up to the Cubs one inning and came back to the dugout and sat down," pitcher Chad Patrick recalled. "Then, I hear Murph."

'WHO WE GOT WARMING UP? BECAUSE PATRICK JUST BLEW THE F---ING GAME.'

"That sat with me for a minute. But it's kind of funny to go back and laugh about."

Patrick recounted that anecdote after being asked for his favorite Murphy interaction. If being called out in front of your team is his favorite, what are the bad moments like?

"It shocks them at first," a Brewers coach said. "Everyone will say it on Twitter tonight. He's just saying it ahead of time."

But there is a method to Murphy's methods, according to those who have worked around him for a long time. Some of it, of course, is about accountability. But perhaps the real secret to the Brewers' success comes down to players knowing what's expected of them before things go wrong.

"It's just setting standards," GM Matt Arnold said. "The bar to be in this dugout is very high."

'The guy has a big heart but bigger expectations'

Former Brewers first baseman Eric Thames didn't like making outs. Sometimes, his displeasure would spill over into the dugout, according to coaches who were in Milwaukee during his three seasons with the team. One time, Thames got jammed and sawed off half his bat while the ball gently landed in the pitcher's glove for the easiest of outs.

Thames came back to the dugout full of vigor, with the remnants of the bat in his hand. Murphy -- then Milwaukee's bench coach -- looked up at him.

"Did you break it?" Murphy deadpanned.

The line drew laughs and calmed Thames. Unlike Patrick's needling, Murphy went in the other direction. He did the same with 21-year-old rookie Luis Lara in a game against the Cubs earlier this year. As Chicago made a pitching change ahead of Lara's at-bat, Murphy put his arms around him, giving him a motivational pep talk. All positive. Moments later, Lara delivered a winning, walk-off single.

"That's my favorite [interaction]," Lara said recently. "It was nice of him."

But Murphy also went the other way in telling Andrew Vaughn he would tase him if he ever got thrown out at third base, as he did in his first few days with the team last year. That carrot-and-stick approach describes Murphy well.

"Sometimes, you have to read between the lines a little bit," closer Trevor Megill said. "The guy has a big heart but bigger expectations."

Bauers added: "It's not an act. That is Murph. Everything he does is coming from a genuine place. The positive and the negative. Sometimes, it can be uncomfortable. If you take it seriously enough, he'll get the best out of you."

Throughout the clubhouse, players pointed to the other end of that spectrum: If taken the right way, Murphy will bring out the best in a player or team.

"He demands excellence," starter Logan Henderson said. "The standard is set so high. It's cool to play for."

But it's not for everyone. Without divulging names, Brewers officials acknowledge some players who have been moved because they couldn't handle it over the years. What has remained is a hardened team that keeps improving year after year, until now finally reaching the cusp of the ultimate goal.

Murphy's presence, humor, discipline and standard set the tone.

"We had a team meeting before the playoffs," pitcher Shane Drohan said. "He started out saying, 'This is the last time we're going to meet.'

"We've had about three team meetings since then. That's Murph."

stories.headline: From an ACL tear to a time trial PB: Koby LeCras on building resilience in his draft year
stories.summary: Rangey wing-forward Koby LeCras saw a breakout year derailed by a partially torn ACL, but six weeks back running was enough to deliver a personal-best 2km time. He talks to Jasper Chellappah about his recovery and future ahead of the 2026 AFL Draft.
stories.body:
Koby LeCras wasn't expected to test at the AFL Draft combine. He also wasn't expected to be named best afield amongst the premier prospects of the 2026 draft class, or make his senior WAFL debut in his dad's No. 20 for West Perth.

It was a blazing start to his season that put the nephew of former West Coast forward Mark firmly in first-round contention. From there it all unravelled.

LeCras suffered a partially torn ACL in that WAFL debut. Senior football, the national championships, and flag tilts were all wiped away. It was a cruel end to a year that promised so much.

But the teenager was desperate to get back for something on his calendar, and the final destination for all draft hopefuls is the combine.

Despite just six weeks of training post-injury, LeCras turned out for the 2km time trial. He ran a 6:23, good for a top-15 time and a personal best under heavy duress.

"Going into it I had 6:25 written on my hand, so I got away with a couple seconds," LeCras told ESPN.

"When I started running it was the goal to do the 2km and the 20m sprint at the combine. I knew what the plan was, where I was going to be and what I was going to do."

Worries had been lurking at the back of Lecras's mind. He avoided surgery on the partial tear but it was difficult for him to regain 100% confidence in his knee when he got back to running.

"You look at Gryan Miers, you can rush it back. Being your draft year and you've obviously got a lot more footy to play than just this year [West Perth] were pretty quick to shut that down, that I wasn't going to play again.

"I just wanted to get back as quick as I could, whether it was combine or day one of pre-season. They said 'Yeah you can do the combine and then definitely back for day one of pre-season'."

LeCras's injury was devastating timing given the showing he'd treated recruiters to the previous week. Off a wing, the 192cm utility was best afield for the AFL Academy - a representative side featuring the best of the draft class thrown together against VFL opposition.

LeCras kicked three goals from 19 disposals and nine marks, commanding the air and showing off that aerobic endurance in defence and attack.

It was a performance reminiscent of Ollie Dempsey's ability to capitalise on mismatches with his strong hands in marking contests and sniff out opportunities in dangerous areas.

LeCras was delivering on the next evolution of the winger in the AFL, but he was playing up the ground out of team need and still sees himself as a forward 50 threat.

"I think I'm a natural forward, but I'm open to playing anywhere, whether it's halfback, wing, hopefully inside one day maybe.

"I love watching specific players, I'm probably a bit of a nuff.

"I love watching Jeremy Cameron, I reckon he's a superstar. And then obviously Logan Morris as well, sort of that undersized key forward. I love what he does and how he finds ways to beat his defenders. He's a freak, he's next level."

Koby's uncle Mark LeCras is one of the more underrated small forwards to play in the modern era. The one club player booted 441 goals from 219 games, and was the oldest player in the Eagles's 2018 triumph before retiring.

Similarly to his uncle, Koby is adept at twisting onto his preferred left foot and finding the goals from uncanny positions. He possesses natural forward craft, from leading patterns at challenging size to match up on to a natural, repeatable set shot action and goal nous from tight angles.

While his dad Brent enjoyed his own 141-game WAFL career, Koby's uncle continues to be a wealth of information as he prepares to step up to the AFL level.

"He's been massive. In the pre-season I watched a lot of vision with him, little ways to improve my game," LeCras said.

"If I could be half the player he was, I'd be really happy with that."

Mark's best day came against Essendon in 2010 at Etihad Stadium, kicking 12 goals straight. He booted 46 goals from 15 games against the Bombers in his career.

"We always joke about that, if he played against Essendon every week he would've kicked a thousand. That's what he reckons!"

stories.headline: Wings' Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd talk relationship on pod
stories.summary: Azzi Fudd hosted Wings teammate Paige Bueckers on her podcast and the two discussed their relationship, Dallas' season and Fudd's recovery from knee surgery.
stories.body:
Dallas Wings teammates Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers, the past two WNBA No. 1 draft picks, spoke on Fudd's podcast Friday about a variety of topics, including a personal life update.

"We're not together anymore; it's been a while," Bueckers said on the "Fudd Around and Find Out" podcast. "[We] share that because everybody [was] like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

Bueckers and Fudd, who were teammates in college at UConn, said they felt the need to address their relationship status in part because of allegations it factored into the Wings picking Fudd at No. 1 in April. Fudd was chosen over TCU guard Olivia Miles, who went on to be the Rookie of the Year for the Minnesota Lynx. Spain's Awa Fam (Seattle Storm) was taken third, followed by teammates from the 2026 champion UCLA Bruins: Lauren Betts (Washington Mystics), Gabriela Jaquez (Chicago Sky) and Kiki Rice (Toronto Tempo).

Fudd, Fam, Betts and Miles were all No. 1 at different points in ESPN's mock draft in the months before the April draft. Bueckers said her previous relationship with Fudd had no impact on Dallas' decision.

"We were not together before she got drafted," Bueckers said. "She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it. She's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player. And we're still friends, we're still cool.

"We played an entire season together; we're the utmost professionals."

Fudd averaged 13.1 points but was limited to just 30 games after an injury to her right knee led to season-ending arthroscopic surgery in August. She offered an update on her health.

"My offseason's been good," Fudd said. "Lots of rehab, lots of training, lots of on-court workouts, lots of traveling. It's been busy.

"I think there's a lot I can improve on. Especially the iso game; I feel like I'm not too comfortable with that yet. I know I'm capable of doing a little bit more. Watching someone like Paige who is able to create from anywhere ... that's great inspiration for me."

Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists, and was named to the All-WNBA second team as Dallas reached the playoffs as the No. 7 seed.

The Wings were eliminated in the first round by the eventual champion Golden State Valkyries. Bueckers said she learned a lot from her first playoff experience and complimented Golden State.

"The Valkyries' defense, I can't explain to you how tough they are," Bueckers said. "They swarm, they send bodies, they trap you, they blitz you, they're so connected. I'm glad I got to have that experience against them to open my eyes to what the playoffs are like -- the physicality, the pressure, the environment.

"And I'm proud of our season. I hated losing; I sat and was pissed about it for like a week. I reached out to [Sue Bird] about it, what was her first playoff experience like. I didn't play as well as I wanted to. But it was my first experience, going against a really good opponent, and I was learning and growing through it all."

Fudd and Bueckers also addressed the Wings' move to the 19,000-seat American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas next season after playing at UT Arlington's College Park Center, which seats over 7,000, since the franchise relocated to Texas in 2016.

"UTA was a vibe; we had a ball, we did our thing there," Bueckers said. "But definitely excited to move into Dallas. New times."

While the change in venue will lead to more eyes on Wings games, the two players said they're hoping for less scrutiny of any on-court behavior.

Both said fans shouldn't read into interactions the two have with each other or their teammates as anything other than normal team behavior. They also said they don't stand for "hate of any kind" or "tearing people down to lift us up."

"We've seen a lot of negativity," Bueckers said. "We've had stuff sent to us, stuff sent to our family, our friends. There's been some crazy things said about us. We still support each other, we're still going to be great friends, we're still going to be great teammates. All the negative things can be put aside, and you don't need to overanalyze everything."

Fudd added with a chuckle, "Also, we don't need messages [from fans] on what the other person's doing. We've addressed everything we need to, and the rest will stay with us."

stories.headline: Jillaroos make shock halves call for World Cup final
stories.summary: Brisbane's Jesse Southwell has replaced Jocelyn Kelleher in the Jillaroos side for the World Cup final as New Zealand make one key change to their men's team.
stories.body:
Australia have recalled Brisbane star Jesse Southwell at five-eighth and dropped Sydney Roosters premiership winner Jocelyn Kelleher for the Women's World Cup final.

It is a big call by Jillaroos coach Jess Skinner ahead of the showdown with the Kiwi Ferns on Sunday at Suncorp Stadium, after Kelleher played in three of the four matches won by Australia in the tournament.

Kelleher was also player of the match at No.6 in the 40-0 win over Samoa on Test debut in the opening round.

Southwell, who will partner Tarryn Aiken in the halves, did shine in the record-breaking 124-6 win over Wales where she had a personal haul of 44 points from a try and 20 goals from 21 attempts.

She was also a key in NSW's 3-0 series win over Queensland in this year's State of Origin series.

Kelleher also kicks goals and shared a strong bond with Roosters teammate and halfback Aiken during their NRLW title win, but has been named in the 21 jersey for the clash with New Zealand.

Try whiz Jaime Chapman has been picked on the wing, despite coming from the field early with a hamstring issue in the 30-14 win over Fiji in the semi-final.

The Ferns have retained the same 17 that defeated Samoa 32-0 in their semi.

New Zealand men's team, meantime, have recalled winger Ronaldo Mulitalo from suspension to the starting side for the final showdown with Australia on Sunday night.

Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad has made way after he scored a try in the 34-10 semi-final win over Tonga.

Mulitalo was sent off in the 72-0 win over Fiji for a shoulder charge and copped a one-match ban.

Australia have named the same 19 that beat Samoa 44-12 for the decider.

Centre Latrell Mitchell and half Sam Walker have been listed at No.18 and No.19 respectively with coach Kevin Walters settling on Bradman Best as his left centre and Tom Dearden at No.7, both of whom were outstanding against Samoa.

Most hockey fans would consider the Avalanche a stronger team this season than the Maple Leafs; nevertheless, Toronto took the opening matchup between these clubs 6-3 on Oct. 10 in Denver.

What should we expect this time around?

The Avs have the NHL's No. 3 offense (4.00 goals per game), led by superstar Nathan MacKinnon (10 goals and 20 assists through 18 games), while Artturi Lehkonen has notched the most goals (12).

Toronto is 12th (3.37 goals per game), led by superstar Auston Matthews (11 goals, 16 assists through 19 games), who is tied for the goal lead with William Nylander.

Both teams are in the middle 10 in goal suppression, so another game with nine combined goals does not seem like a far-fetched projection!

Minnesota Wild at Montreal Canadiens

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -118, O/U: 6.5

For a variety of reasons a Stanley Cup Final pairing with these two teams would be electric.

Each team features stars both established and rising, two of the sport's elite young netminders, and there could be some leftover animosity toward Wild GM Bill Guerin on the part of Montreal's Cole Caufield and Lane Hutson, who were snubs from the 2026 Olympic roster.

Currently, Stathletes gives this a 1.00% chance of happening as the Final matchup this coming spring, which is 30th highest.

In addition to Caufield and Hutson, Nick Suzuki -- the reigning Selke Trophy winner -- is a player to watch for Montreal.

Minnesota is led by Kirill Kaprizov (tied for the league lead with 16 goals), Quinn Hughes (second in scoring among defenseman) and Jesper Wallstedt, who is tied for the league lead with 11 wins and is top five in both goals-against average and save percentage.

Washington Capitals at Ottawa Senators

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -130, O/U: 6.5

Until the NHL expands to an additional international market, this is the only matchup between national capital cities. And, these two teams should be battling for playoff position right until the end of the season.

The big news for Ottawa is that goaltender Linus Ullmark was activated from injured reserve on Sunday, and could return to the Senators' crease for this contest. Prior to his injury, he had a 7-1-0 record, 1.33 GAA and .945 SV%; needless to say, his presence will be a game changer.

Up front, Tim Stutzle is on pace for 107 points, which would be a career high by 17.

The Capitals have not gotten that kind of play out of either Logan Thompson or Charlie Lindgren, so they'll have to continue outscoring their goal-suppression shortcomings. Offseason additions Jordan Kyrou (14 points in 15 games) and Alex Tuch (11 goals) are helping on that front.

New Jersey Devils at Winnipeg Jets

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ -142, O/U: 5.5

Ah, what could have been. Unlike when Brady Tkachuk returned to Ottawa or Quinn Hughes to Vancouver, Hellebuyck will not be heavily involved in game play when his new team returns to his old home. How will the fans know when to boo?

Nevertheless, they will still play the game on Tuesday with or without Hellebuyck. The Devils enter the game in second place in the Metro Division, winners of five straight. The Jets are sixth in the Central, and have three W's in a row.

Jack Hughes leads the group playing in front of Jake Allen for Jersey, with 25 points through 18 games. Kyle Connor (19 points in 18 games) is Winnipeg's leading scorer, a point ahead of Mark Scheifele.

Florida Panthers at Columbus Blue Jackets

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+/Disney+/Hulu) | CBJ -110, O/U: 5.5

This will be the second game of the season between these two clubs. Florida won the first back on Oct. 13 by a touchdown to a field goal.

Brady Tkachuk has not wasted any time making a name for himself as a Panther, with two fights in the regular season and one in the preseason (no, seriously), as well as 10 goals through 18 games. His 20 points are six back of brother Matthew for the team lead.

The host Blue Jackets are led by a leveled-up Kent Johnson, who is on pace for 45 goals and 90 points for the full season; those would smash his career highs (24 and 57, respectively). And of course, Columbus also employs Zach Werenski, the 2026 Norris Trophy winner who leads all players this season with 28:17 in ice time per game.

Detroit Red Wings at St. Louis Blues

8 p.m. ET (TNT) | STL -142, O/U: 5.5

An old-school rivalry from the black 'n' blue days of the Norris Division. Sadly, given that these teams are in different conferences now this will be the final game they play against one another (unless they meet in the Cup Final).

In Game 1 of the season series, the Blues earned the 5-4 win on Halloween, with the teams combining for 51 hits but only 10 penalty minutes. Nine different players scored a goal in that contest; might that feat be repeated here?

It was an unusually rough outing for St. Louis goalie Joel Hofer, who is experiencing a breakout this season. After John Gibson allowed five Blues goals on 15 shots, might Detroit tap Daniil Tarasov for this one -- particularly given his sparkling 2.10 GAA and .919 SV%?

Nashville Predators at Los Angeles Kings

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+/Disney+/Hulu) | LA -142, O/U: 5.5

This is the first meeting between two teams that should be right in the mix for a wild-card spot out West this spring.

After a six-game losing streak to start the season, the Kings have gone 5-4-0 since, which is a better nine-game stretch than a lot of other teams can claim out there! Artemi Panarin is the premier superstar for the Kings up front, and his 18 points through 15 game have him on a 101-point pace by season's end.

The Preds had a slightly better start to the season, but more importantly they've won four straight coming into this contest; that includes W's over three of the top Cup contenders -- Tampa, Carolina and Colorado. Roman Josi and Filip Forsberg are tied for the team scoring lead with 20 points in 17 games, which puts them on a 99-point pace. Steven Stamkos has 10 goals in 17 games, which puts him just a hair below 50-goal pace for the season.

Of the most "unbreakable" records in sports, Hockey Hall of Fame goaltender Glenn Hall might have the ultimate one -- and there's a tie-in to today's date in hockey history.

On Nov. 10, 1962, Hall didn't play in the Chicago Blackhawks' game against the Montreal Canadiens, which ended his streak of starting 502 consecutive regular-season games. Including playoff games, his streak was 552 consecutive starts.

stories.headline: Man United executives, Sir Jim Ratcliffe meeting to discuss Carrick future - sources
stories.summary: Manchester United executives are meeting with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe this week to discuss Michael Carrick's future as head coach, sources have told ESPN.
stories.body:
Manchester United executives are meeting with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe this week to discuss Michael Carrick's future as head coach, sources have told ESPN.

Carrick is on the brink of the sack after overseeing a miserable start to the season which has included just one league win.

Club sources insist a final decision has not yet been taken, but the 45-year-old is increasingly likely to lose his job before United return to action after the international break against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22.

The meeting in Monaco, which will include CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, was pre-planned and has not been called in response to a dire run of form which has seen United slip in the Premier League's relegation places. However, Carrick's future is set to dominate the agenda.

Berrada and Wilcox discussed the situation during talks on Monday.

Carrick and his staff had the day off following Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. Carrick returned to Carrington on Tuesday morning and is said to be carrying on as normal. The majority of the squad are on international duty with their respective nations.

Mauricio Pochettino, Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte are among the names in the frame to come in if Ratcliffe backs a recommendation from Berrada and Wilcox to replace Carrick.

Former Ipswich Town manager Kieran McKenna, who was interviewed for the job in 2024, has admirers internally, although one source has told ESPN that United's predicament means it was unlikely they would target a young, up-and-coming coach.

- Man United executives, Sir Jim Ratcliffe meeting to discuss Carrick future - sources

- Sir Jim Ratcliffe chose to appoint rookies at Man United, and it has them facing relegation﻿ fight
